extracted.intended_audience: Authors preparing and submitting manuscripts to BMC Research Notes (Springer Nature)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing, formatting, licensing, and submitting manuscripts (research notes, data notes, commentaries, etc.) to BMC Research Notes, including data/figure/table requirements, peer review expectations, and APC/licensing information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims and scope / suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure you submit to the most suitable journal. BMC Research Notes is an open access journal publishing peer-reviewed contributions across scientific and clinical disciplines, including initial observations, updates, established methods, valid negative results, and scientific datasets and descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should confirm their manuscript fits the journal’s remit (health sciences, biology, physical sciences, community topics such as bioethics, data publishing, education, methodology, metascience, etc.) before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission must be by an author (no third-party submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A manuscript can only be submitted by an author of the manuscript and may not be submitted by a third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure one of the paper’s authors completes the submission; do not use agents or third-party submitters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article processing charge (APC) and pricing policy
rubrics_metrics.description: An APC applies for each article accepted for publication. Current APC for BMC Research Notes is £1240.00 GBP / $1790.00 USD / €1490.00 EUR (subject to VAT/local taxes). Springer Nature operates country-tiered APC pricing pilot which may affect charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: APC is determined from the acceptance date; check APC applicable to your country, available institutional agreements, and whether discretionary waivers/discounts apply (apply at submission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access licensing options and implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles are published under Creative Commons licences: CC BY-NC-ND (non-commercial, no derivatives) or CC BY (allows adaptation and commercial use) and authors retain copyright.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a licence consistent with funder/institution requirements; CC BY-NC-ND restricts commercial re-use and adaptations, CC BY allows broad re-use with attribution. Learn about licence variations if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand open access funding/discount/waiver procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer Nature offers institutional agreements to cover OA costs; discounts and waivers available for corresponding authors in lowest-income countries; other waiver requests considered case-by-case and must be applied for at submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check institutional eligibility, funder support, and submit waiver/discount requests at the point of manuscript submission (requests during review or after acceptance cannot be considered).

rubrics_metrics.name: General manuscript formatting: spacing, numbering, units, characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Use double-line spacing; include line and page numbering; use SI units; ensure special characters are embedded in the text; do not use page breaks in your manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embedding characters prevents loss during PDF conversion. Avoid manual page breaks which can interfere with production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable main manuscript file formats and requirement for editable files
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptable formats: Microsoft Word (DOC, DOCX), Rich Text Format (RTF), TeX/LaTeX. Editable files are required for processing; non-editable files (such as PDFs) will require resubmission of editable source if included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit editable source files with initial submission. If non-editable files are present, be prepared to re-submit editable versions during revision or after acceptance to avoid production delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX/TeX submission specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to use the Springer Nature LaTeX template. A PDF will be compiled using pdfLaTeX and TexLive 2021. All relevant editable source files must be uploaded; failing to submit source files will cause delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include all source files during submission (style files, bibliographies, figures, etc.) so production can compile without requesting missing components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and materials expectation and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All BioMed Central journals strongly encourage or require authors to provide datasets on which conclusions rely. Datasets should be deposited in public repositories where appropriate or presented in the main paper or additional supporting files, in machine-readable formats (spreadsheets rather than PDFs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where community norms mandate repository archiving, submission to a recognized public repository is mandatory. Provide data availability details in the 'Availability of data and materials' section; avoid linking to personal/departmental websites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and wording for 'Availability of data and materials' section
rubrics_metrics.description: The Availability section should state where supporting datasets are available and include unique persistent identifiers and hyperlinks in https:// format, or state when data are included as additional files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required example formats: "The dataset(s) supporting the conclusions of this article is(are) available in the [repository name] repository, [unique persistent identifier and hyperlink to dataset(s) in https:// format]." Or: "...included within the article (and its additional file(s))." Include accession numbers/DOIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data citation and repository guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: BioMed Central endorses the Force 11 Data Citation Principles and requires that all publicly available datasets be fully referenced in the reference list with an accession number or unique identifier (e.g., DOI). For databases, state web/ftp address and any use restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite datasets in references; follow community repository expectations; for clinical data or restricted datasets, follow editorial policies for disclosure and access restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software metadata requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For software, the 'Availability' section should include project name, project home page, archived version DOI/identifier, operating system(s), programming language, other requirements, license, and any restrictions to use by non-academics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough metadata (example fields given) so other researchers can find, run and cite the software; include archived version DOI (e.g., Zenodo) where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference inclusion rules (what to cite)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only articles, clinical trial registration records and abstracts that have been published or are in press, or are available through public e-print/preprint servers, may be cited in the reference list. Unpublished abstracts, unpublished data and personal communications should not be included in the reference list but may be mentioned in text as 'unpublished observations' or 'personal communications' (with permission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain permission to quote personal communications; include names of involved researchers. Only footnotes are permitted. Provide in-press articles if requested by editorial office for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference formatting and web link rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the Instructions for Authors for the relevant reference style. All web links and URLs, including to authors' own websites, should be given a reference number and included in the reference list (not in-text), provided in full with title, URL, and date accessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example format provided. Authors may use reference management software to ensure correct formatting. If an author/group can be associated with a web link (e.g., weblog), include the author in the reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure numbering, composite figures, and file handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be numbered in the order first mentioned. Multi-panel figures should be submitted as a single composite file containing all parts. Figures must be uploaded in correct orientation; figure titles (max 15 words) and legends (max 300 words) should be provided in the main manuscript, not in the graphic file. Figure keys should be in the graphic, not the legend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crop figures closely to minimise white space. Provide titles and legends in the manuscript text so they are searchable and editable during production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable figure file types, file sizes, resolution and design rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted figure file formats: EPS, PDF, Microsoft Word (single page), PowerPoint (single page), TIFF, JPEG, PNG, BMP, CDX (ChemDraw). Individual figure files should not exceed 10 MB. Figures on the web: width 600 px (standard) or 1200 px (high resolution). PDF final sizes: half page width 85 mm, full page width 170 mm, max height 225 mm. Image resolution ~300 dpi at final size. All fonts must be embedded; all lines wider than 0.25 pt at standard widths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vector figures are best as PDF. TIFF files should use LZW compression. JPEGs saved at maximum quality. Minimise conversion between file types to avoid quality loss. Ensure text and lines remain legible at final sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for previously published figures/tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must obtain permission from the copyright holder to reproduce figures or tables previously published elsewhere. For inclusion in open access article, permission is required for items published previously in non-open access journals. Permission should be indicated in the figure legend and original source included in reference list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to obtain and document permissions may prevent inclusion of reused material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table formatting, numbering, placement and content rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables should be numbered and cited in sequence using Arabic numerals. Tables less than one A4/Letter page can be placed within the manuscript; larger tables can be placed at the end or uploaded as additional files (Excel or CSV). Table titles (max 15 words) above the table; legends (max 300 words) underneath. Tables should be formatted using the 'Table object' function in the word processor (not as embedded figures/spreadsheets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use color or shading. Use superscript, numbering, lettering, symbols or bold text to highlight, and explain meanings in the legend. Do not use commas to indicate numerical values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional files policy and formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may provide datasets, tables, movies, or other information as additional files; all additional files will be published with the accepted article. Do not include patient consent forms, certificates of language editing, or revised versions of the main manuscript with tracked changes as additional files unless requested. Maximum file size for additional files is 20 MB each; files are virus-scanned on submission. Each additional file should be cited in sequence within the main text and named 'Additional file 1' etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each additional file, list filename, file format (with correct extension), title of data, and description of data in a separate section of the manuscript text. Use Excel (.xls) or .csv for tabular additional files. Avoid linking to personal sites; deposit in recognised repositories where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language quality and editing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting work in well-written English gives the best chance for editors and reviewers to understand and evaluate it fairly. Use tutorials, ask native colleagues, or use professional language editing services if needed. Springer Nature Author Services and partner tools (e.g., AJE language quality checker) are available but not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using an editing service is optional and does not guarantee editorial selection or acceptance. Tools such as the AJE language checker can give fast feedback but are not a substitute for substantive editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter contents and supporting information at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover letter should include: an explanation of why your manuscript should be published in BMC Research Notes; explanation of any issues relating to journal policies; declaration of potential competing interests; confirmation all authors have approved the manuscript for submission; confirmation content has not been published or submitted elsewhere. If submitting to a special issue, refer to its specific name. Authors may suggest peer reviewers and list those they prefer not to review the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If suggesting reviewers provide institutional email addresses or identity-verifying information (e.g., ORCID or Scopus ID). Intentionally falsifying reviewer information will result in rejection and possible misconduct investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review criteria used to assess manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically two or more experts evaluate each manuscript based on three main criteria: scientific robustness (is methodology sound and do data support conclusions?), originality (does the research duplicate existing work?), and clarity (is the manuscript clear and coherent enough for publication?).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors make decisions based on reviewers' reports and may consult the editorial board. Reviewers and editors are required to declare competing interests; they may be excluded if a conflict exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent peer review option and reviewer anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: BMC Research Notes operates a transparent peer review system: if the article is published, reviewer reports are published online alongside the article under a Creative Commons Attribution License 4.0, but the reviewer is not named.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and reviewers should be aware reviews may be published (anonymously) and this can aid transparency and education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript transfer process and Transfer Desk support
rubrics_metrics.description: If a manuscript is not accepted in the chosen journal, authors may be offered transfer to another journal within the Springer Nature portfolio. Transfer offers provide options, save time (no reformatting necessary), and may use the Transfer Desk to match manuscripts to suitable journals combining author preferences and editor recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers require author agreement to proceed; files and reviewer comments can be resubmitted. Authors may decline or withdraw transfers at any point by contacting the Transfer Desk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion and dissemination encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer Nature promotes individual articles through marketing channels (emails, homepage posts, social media, blogs, press releases) and encourages authors to promote their work via email, social media, conferences, and institutional channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to actively disseminate their work to increase views, downloads and impact, alongside publisher promotion.
